cells.tense: You are holding the pen on what is fair between people here.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Pick one arrangement between you and another person that has finished. Mark it done and let your half go, without a verdict. Then see what stays warm.
cells.core:
Down here in the body, you can feel a thing all the way through and still land on what's fair. Not fairness that tabs up columns. Fairness that has sat with the whole mess and come out steady, and the people in it can tell the difference.

What came to you is release, done on purpose. So look at something between you and another person that already ended. Not a friendship you're sore about. An arrangement, a way of trading, a version of the deal that stopped fitting and you've kept honoring from habit. Finish it quietly, on your own end, and clear a little of the done thing. Watch how much room is left, and how much more of you stands in it. What they brought you gets set down here, and what's got life in it stays.
cells.sheetLine: You feel the whole thing and still set down what's finished.
cells.verb: weighing what's fair while the feeling is still running
cells.place: at a threshold where what's held gets set down on purpose

cells.tense: You will brace for a ruling that has not arrived yet, pen moving already.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Hold your verdict for a day when a thing between you and another person goes crooked. Say nothing yet. Then set out a single next step you can see, and take that one alone.
cells.core:
Fairness is still your ground, and here it runs ahead of itself. A thing goes off balance between you and another person, and you've already decided what's right before either of you has finished feeling it. Not out of hardness. Out of knowing, too far in advance. And the verdict lands, and it lands heavy, and the person under it hears a court, not a friend.

What's left in you is the plain strength of a builder. So carry the crooked thing for a day without a ruling. Just hold it. Then find a step you can actually see, lay it down solid, and take that one. Stone doesn't move itself, and neither does the call.

cells.tense: You were fair in this part of life once, and that time sits behind you.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Write the facts of an unfairness you've stopped naming, in order, one thing then the next, no feeling words. Read the page back and change nothing on it.
cells.core:
A thing between people went crooked and the fair call didn't come. It could have. You had the eye for it. But it stayed unmade, and the skewed thing sits there, and the ones living beside it quit waiting on you to say what's what. Not a failure of heart. A door you walked past, and you facing the other way.

Here the ground back isn't feeling; it's method. On the page, write what happened the way you'd write a report, one thing after another, no mood words anywhere in it. Then read it back. Nothing to decide, no one to tell. The record in your handwriting says what the unspoken sentence couldn't, and it says it in your order.

cells.tense: You are keeping things level among your people without noticing the work.
cells.act: perceive it with fresh eyes before judging
cells.ask: Listen through the next squabble near you like you're new here, before you smooth anything. Take in all of it, decide nothing, then leave it where it lands.
cells.core:
Among the people close to you, weights stay where they should. A word shifted here, a tone softened there, and the room comes out even. That's your hand, and if someone asked, you'd say you weren't in it. Here's what's true: the ones being kept level have known the whole time. They just didn't need it named.

So before you reach in next time and even the thing out the way you do, hear it first. Take in the whole squabble the way someone new to it would, without deciding who's right. You'll catch the part that usually gets smoothed before anyone says it. Nothing changes except that you'll have seen your own hand, from the inside, once.

attempts.check: The seat's power in the record is a capacity, but nothing supports saying the person has already lost anything, so every cell describes what their fairness is doing now, not what they gave up. A reader could object that I've made the release sound like a duty rather than something already happening, and they'd be right to say so; the asks stay useful even if my read of which feeling is stale is wrong, because closing a finished arrangement is ordinary maintenance either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying their calm is a performance — cut it.
